title: Finite-level pro-etale compact-support base change
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring, and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\ f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\ Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y\end{array}$$
be a compact-support base-change square [def-cbc-compact-support-square], with $f:X\to Y$ separated of finite type and $g:Y'\to Y$ arbitrary [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Assume that $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, or that a compactification $c=(j,p)$ of $f$ is given. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\Proet},\Lambda)$ carry an etale-origin witness $(L,\alpha)$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], with the constant discrete coefficient categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules].

Choose $c$ (a Nagata compactification when only the qcqs hypothesis is supplied) and its base change $c'=(j',p')$. Use the compactification formulas $Rf_!^{c,e}=Rp_*^e j_!^e$, $Rf_!^{c,p}=Rp_*^p j_!^p$, and their primed analogues, with operations as in [def-cbc-exchange-map, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. The pro-etale exchange
$$g_{\Proet}^{-1}Rf_!^{c,p}K\longrightarrow Rf'_!^{c',p}g'_{\Proet}{}^{-1}K$$
is the etale compactification exchange of [def-cbc-exchange-map] transported through the proper/open comparison and the pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] to etale-origin objects, then conjugated by $\alpha$. It is an isomorphism. It is independent of the witness and independent of $c$ under the transported canonical compactification comparisons supplied by [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]. Full faithfulness on $D^+$ is [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]. No constructibility or residue-characteristic assumption, and no qcqs assumption on $Y'$, is made.

proof.text: If a compactification is supplied, take it. Otherwise $Y$ is qcqs and [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies $c=(j,p)$. For either case, [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target] applied to $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ shows that $j$ is quasi-compact: $f=pj$ is finite type and proper $p$ is separated. Thus this is a derived compact-support compactification without a new hypothesis on $j$. [def-cbc-compact-support-square] supplies its pullback $c'=(j',p')$, with $p'$ proper and $j'$ open. Properness means separated and finite type by [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; hence $p,p'$ are quasi-compact, and [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] makes them quasi-separated. These are relative qcqs properties of the proper maps; they do not require $Y'$ to be qcqs.

source.place: Opening compactification choice, with the human-authorized qcqs-or-compactification repair of 2026-10-18

proof.text:
The witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] gives $L\in D^+(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\alpha:\nu_X^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}K$. Apply [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] to $f$, $c$ and arbitrary $g$: step 1 proved the required quasi-compactness of $j$. This gives the natural isomorphism
$$E^c_L:g_e^{-1}H_c^eL\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{c'}^eg_e'{}^{-1}L,\qquad H_c^e=Rp_*^ej_!^e,$$
which is precisely the proper-exchange followed by extension-by-zero composite of [def-cbc-exchange-map]. Put $M=g_e'{}^{-1}L$. The exact constant-module inverse image in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] implies that $M$ remains bounded below. The compactification-independence clause of the same finite-torsion theorem will be used in step 8, not a Zariski extension of this formula.

source.place: Etale finite-torsion theorem on the global compactification

proof.text:
Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$. Exactness of $A_T$ is [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level]. Etale extension by zero preserves quasi-isomorphisms and acts degreewise by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and pro-etale extension by zero is exact and degreewise by [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]. For a representative complex $C$ of $L$, apply the natural sheaf comparison of [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] in each degree. Naturality with respect to $d_C^n$ says the resulting components commute with the differentials; their inverses do too. This gives a chain isomorphism $e_{j,L}:A_{\bar X}j_!^eL\simeq j_!^pA_XL$, independent of the representative, since all functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. In particular $j_!^eL$ stays bounded below. Take $b_p$ to be the specified canonical counit-mate direct-image comparison normalized in [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange], not an arbitrary choice of isomorphism; its underlying natural isomorphism is [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image]. Combine it with $e_j$ to obtain
$$C_{c,L}:A_Y Rf_!^{c,e}L=A_YRp_*^ej_!^eL\xrightarrow{b_{p,j_!L}}Rp_*^pA_{\bar X}j_!^eL\xrightarrow{Rp_*^p(e_{j,L})}Rf_!^{c,p}A_XL.$$
Both arrows are isomorphisms, natural in $L$. For $M=g_e'{}^{-1}L$, the base-changed formula is explicitly
$$C_{c',M}:A_{Y'}Rp'_*^ej'_!^eM\xrightarrow{b_{p',j'_!M}}Rp'_*^pA_{\bar X'}j'_!^eM\xrightarrow{Rp'_*^p(e_{j',M})}Rp'_*^pj'_!^pA_{X'}M.$$
Here $M$ is bounded below because etale inverse image is exact, as in [def-cbc-exchange-map]; the degreewise natural comparison for $j'$ gives $e_{j',M}$ and the qcqs map $p'$ gives $b_{p'}$.

source.place: Tags 09A6 (lemma-morphism-comparison) and 09AF (lemma-jshriek-comparison); degreewise derived comparison as in the blueprint transport paragraph

proof.text:
Write $H_c^p=Rp_*^pj_!^p$ and $H_{c'}^p=Rp'_*^pj'_!^p$. Let $a_u:A_Uu_e^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}u_p^{-1}A_V$ be [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Using the natural isomorphisms $C_{c,L}$ and $C_{c',M}$ from step 3, set
$$S^c_L=g_p^{-1}(C_{c,L})\circ a_{g,H_c^eL},\qquad T^c_L=H_{c'}^p(a_{g',L})\circ C_{c',M}.$$
They identify the endpoints of $A_{Y'}(E^c_L)$ with $g_p^{-1}H_c^pA_XL$ and $H_{c'}^pg_p'{}^{-1}A_XL$. Thus the specified transported exchange is
$$F^c_L=T^c_L\circ A_{Y'}(E^c_L)\circ(S^c_L)^{-1}.$$
This is the transport of the particular composite in [def-cbc-exchange-map]. For its proper factor [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] applies to $p,p'$ and $j_!^eL$ (step 1 supplies relative qcqs and step 3 boundedness), and identifies the specified proper mate. The canonical pro-etale open base-change isomorphism is [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-base-change]. The exchange asserted here is the transported compactification composite, with this normalization; no global-to-chart comparison is needed.

source.place: Transport of the proper/open compactification composite

proof.text:
Every factor of $F^c_L$ is invertible, by steps 2--4, and its inverse is $S^c_LA_{Y'}((E^c_L)^{-1})(T^c_L)^{-1}$. These factors are natural in $L$, so $F^c$ is natural as well: substitute the naturality equalities for $S^c,T^c$ and $E^c$ into the displayed composite. Put $P_c=g_p^{-1}H_c^p$ and $Q_c=H_{c'}^pg_p'{}^{-1}$. The witness [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] gives the exchange on $K$ as
$$\Psi^c_{L,\alpha}=Q_c(\alpha)F^c_LP_c(\alpha)^{-1}.$$
Its inverse is $P_c(\alpha)(F^c_L)^{-1}Q_c(\alpha)^{-1}$, by associativity and inverse cancellation. This proves invertibility of the actual arrow on $K$.

source.place: Transported inverse and conjugation by the witness

proof.text: For another witness $(L',\alpha')$ of $K$, [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] makes $A_X=\nu_X^*$ fully faithful on all of $D^+$, without a constructibility restriction. Apply [lem-cbc-fully-faithful-isomorphism-lift] to $\alpha'^{-1}\alpha:A_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}A_XL'$. It gives the unique isomorphism $u:L\xrightarrow{\sim}L'$ with $A_Xu=\alpha'^{-1}\alpha$, so $\alpha'A_Xu=\alpha$. Naturality established in step 5 gives $F^c_{L'}P_c(A_Xu)=Q_c(A_Xu)F^c_L$.

source.place: Lifting the isomorphism between two etale-origin representatives

proof.text:
Substituting $\alpha'A_Xu=\alpha$ and the naturality equality of step 6 gives
$$\begin{aligned}Q_c(\alpha')F^c_{L'}P_c(\alpha')^{-1}
&=Q_c(\alpha')F^c_{L'}P_c(A_Xu)P_c(\alpha)^{-1}\\
&=Q_c(\alpha')Q_c(A_Xu)F^c_LP_c(\alpha)^{-1}\\
&=Q_c(\alpha)F^c_LP_c(\alpha)^{-1}.\end{aligned}$$
This is equality of the two specified arrows on $K$. It proves independence of every choice of witness, in particular of replacing the witness by an isomorphic one.

source.place: Witness independence by explicit naturality and cancellation

proof.text:
For two compactifications $c,d$, [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] supplies the canonical natural comparisons $r:H_c^e\xrightarrow{\sim}H_d^e$ and $r':H_{c'}^e\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{d'}^e$ and the equality
$$r'_M E^c_L=E^d_L g_e^{-1}(r_L),\qquad M=g_e'{}^{-1}L.$$
Transport their endpoints using step 3: set $D_L=C_{d,L}A_Y(r_L)C_{c,L}^{-1}$ and $D'_M=C_{d',M}A_{Y'}(r'_M)C_{c',M}^{-1}$. On the exchange endpoints put
$$U_L=g_p^{-1}(D_L),\qquad V_L=H_{d'}^p(a_{g',L})D'_M H_{c'}^p(a_{g',L})^{-1}.$$
Naturality of $a_g$ from [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] and cancellation in the definitions give
$$U_LS^c_L=S^d_LA_{Y'}(g_e^{-1}r_L),\qquad V_LT^c_L=T^d_LA_{Y'}(r'_M).$$
Consequently
$$V_LF^c_L=T^d_LA_{Y'}(r'_ME^c_L)(S^c_L)^{-1}=F^d_LU_L.$$
These are exactly the transported canonical compactification comparisons: each is obtained by conjugating the etale comparison by the specified endpoint isomorphisms. They are natural in $L$; conjugating them by $P_c(\alpha),P_d(\alpha)$ and $Q_c(\alpha),Q_d(\alpha)$ gives the same equality for $\Psi^c_{L,\alpha}$ and $\Psi^d_{L,\alpha}$ on $K$. Step 7 makes this transport independent of the witness. Since the etale comparisons are independent of the common refinement, so are their conjugates; the exchanged arrow is therefore independent of $c$ under these canonical identifications.

source.place: Compactification independence: transport the finite-torsion comparison square

proof.text: For the fixed-module auxiliary clause isIso_csAuxiliaryExchange, retain W.complex and W.iso to obtain plusEtaleOrigin for M.obj. The existing source lemma plusEtaleOrigin_mapDerivedCategory_openImmersionLowerShriek applies the termwise open site comparison to show that extension by zero retains this property. Apply the existing fixed-module proper theorem isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap_app_of_isProper to the proper compactification square, via isIso_derivedBaseChangeMap_app_openImmersionLowerShriek_of_compactification. The actual canonicalFiniteCoefficientCompactSupportExchange is its proper component preceded by an associator and followed by the specified open base-change isomorphism. NatTrans.isIso_app_comp_whiskerLeft_comp therefore proves invertibility directly, without identifying the full global transported exchange or choosing an inverse. This proves the auxiliary clause; steps 1--8 remain the proof plan of the reexported global interface.
